findings.english_quote: for peace is dear to him.
findings.issue: The translation faithfully follows the selected ei reading, but the notes do not disclose its editorial status or the supplied apparatus alternative. The attributed apparatus identifies ei as Gebhardt’s conjecture, compares Palatina and Ethiopic support, and reports et in the cited Vulgata manuscripts. The existing note explains the editorial choices in section 4 but leaves this additional conjectural reading undisclosed.
findings.suggested_revision: Retain the selected main-text rendering. Add a brief note stating that “to him” follows the working edition’s conjectural ei; the supplied apparatus reports et (“and”) in the cited Vulgata manuscripts and compares Palatina and Ethiopic support for ei. Attribute this information to the edition’s reported apparatus, not to fresh manuscript verification. Review the proposed note before publication.

findings.suggested_revision: Keep the selected sentence and add an accessible note explaining that “to him” follows the working edition’s editorial reading ei, while the supplied apparatus reports et (“and”) in the cited Vulgata manuscripts and compares support from Palatina and Ethiopic. summary: Both editions preserve the selected source’s substantive clauses, garment–spirit comparison, negations, punishment, dialogue attribution, and contextual repentance. The simplified edition’s compression retains the meaning of the repeated usefulness statements. Both appropriately disclose the section-4 conjecture and bracketed death supplement; the existence of alternatives does not require replacing those working readings. Minor revision is needed to disclose the additional conjectural ei reading in section 2. This assessment concerns the supplied source and attributed reports, not authentication of unseen manuscripts or exhaustive collation.
